quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and lets others see you.
Increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
Increases your chance of hitting road hazards and lets others pass you.
Reduces your chance of hitting road hazards and lets you follow closely behind another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears. Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Signal your intentions with proper use of signals, brake lights, and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and check the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All motorcycle riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should only be used when the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of total braking power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, the body eliminates about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower blood alcohol content varies, so it is safest to not drive any vehicle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to follow at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check over your shoulder regularly as part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: When you sit on your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After sitting on your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:

options.text: How much tread is on your tires.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and surfaces.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: If you need to stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which requires more braking power. Going downhill also makes stopping harder. Both factors combined mean stopping takes much longer.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: You'll have a better chance of avoiding serious injury if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes, and durable gloves.

questions.question: You should do all of the following to reduce your chances of a crash, except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your turns and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, and look for hazards. Don't rely on hoping others see you.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you and spot hazards early.

questions.question: Which formation is best for keeping group riders close together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close together while giving each rider safe space. Use single-file for curves, turns, or entering and exiting highways.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual first. It has all the information you need about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: You should leave more space between you and other vehicles:

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second gap is normally good. Leave extra space when conditions make it harder to stop, like wet or icy roads.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, give clear side views, fasten securely, allow air flow, and have room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: A good lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: See better and be seen better.

questions.explanation: Your position in the lane helps your safety. It helps you see and be seen better, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Should reduce their usual space cushions by half.
Should keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but always keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle feels with the extra weight.
